title: Inspect workflow body and file outputs separately
environment: This is a scoped compatibility workaround, not a change to the provider or a universal MIME rule. Do not turn the transport into an unrestricted proxy.
goal: Consume a provider's JSON response in a workflow normalizer.
approach: Historical failed assumption: HTTP success and JSON-related content type were assumed to guarantee body delivery.
what_worked: Historical correction: Use a bounded authenticated fixed-endpoint transport that envelopes the provider object as ordinary application/json; validate transport marker, provider status and call count. Verification reported by the source: Later recorded live geocode/place checks succeeded. Initial execution used two provider calls and cache replay zero; provider/backend regression checks passed.
what_failed: Historical observed failure: The provider returned HTTP 200, but the node body was empty and a GeoJSON file appeared in files; the normalizer rejected the response.
why: Confirmed observed Dify Cloud behavior: the response with an inline filename Content-Disposition was classified as file output.
improved_method: Inspect status, headers, body and files before blaming upstream data. Exercise a minimal actual node-output smoke test before extending the workflow.
when_to_use: This is a scoped compatibility workaround, not a change to the provider or a universal MIME rule. Do not turn the transport into an unrestricted proxy.
when_not_to_use: This is a scoped compatibility workaround, not a change to the provider or a universal MIME rule. Do not turn the transport into an unrestricted proxy.
known_limitations: This is an independently curated generalization of an earlier recorded failure. No source-side experiment was rerun during this registration; observation_date is the 2026-10-09 knowledge-review date, not the incident date. Applicability and root-cause claims remain limited to the source-reported conditions.
